_meta.title: TV quote index — dweeb.co
_meta.note: Curated famous short lines only. A quote index, NOT a script archive. Episode metadata (season, number, air date) are facts, each cross-checked against multiple reliable sources.
_meta.sources: Wikipedia, Wikidata, Apple TV, TVmaze, IMDb, Peacock, HBO Max, Rotten Tomatoes, Metacritic, Wikisimpsons, TV Tropes
_meta.schema: q = quote, who = character, show = series. Episode-cited rows add: ep (episode title), s (season), e (episode number), aired (original US air date). Video-cited rows add: artist, song. A row has one shape or the other, never both.
rules: Short famous catchphrases only — no extended dialogue, no song lyrics.
Every quote's episode must exist in the verified registry (build script rejects otherwise).
80-character ceiling per quote, enforced by the validator.
All quotes from one episode must carry identical metadata, enforced by the validator.
No recurring catchphrase is included unless the episode is its verified origin.
Music-video commentary rows cite artist + song in place of season/episode. This is not a substitute for provenance — for a video-commentary segment the video IS the provenance.
Validator checks for season/episode SLOT COLLISIONS — two different episode titles claiming the same season+number within one show. This caught a real error in a user-supplied source.

excluded_deliberately.song_lyrics: The Monorail Song, Talkin' Softball — separately credited copyrighted compositions.
recurring_catchphrases_no_home_episode: King of the Hill: 'That boy ain't right', 'I sell propane and propane accessories', 'Bwah!' — Fandom documents these as serieswide catchphrases.
Married... with Children: 'Four touchdowns in one game' — referenced across all 11 seasons; the Al Bundy Store page itself notes it recurs throughout.

Beavis and Butt-Head: 'Fire! Fire!', 'This sucks', 'Huh huh huh' — recur serieswide with no single home episode and no associated video. Cornholio lines ARE included with an episode cite (S4E31 is their verified origin); the 39 music-video one-liners are included with a video cite.
excluded_deliberately.rationale: Per user decision: exclude any catchphrase that cannot be assigned a verifiable episode, rather than assigning a fitting-but-unverified one. The page renders season/episode/air-date as a factual claim indistinguishable from verified entries, so an invented citation would undermine every other row.

source_notes.albundystore.com: User-supplied Al Bundy quote page attaches S/E/title to most lines, which is unusual and useful as a LEAD. It is a merch store blog, not a citation-grade source, and two of its own entries conflict internally (NO MA'AM founding listed as both S7E13 and S9E5). Only its Pilot (S1E1) attributions were used, after independently verifying the episode against Wikipedia, IMDb, Metacritic, Fandom, FoxWorld and Grokipedia.
source_notes.tvdatabase.fandom.com: DISCARDED as a source. Returned mangled/copy-pasted data 5+ times across shows.
source_notes.screenrant.com: User-supplied Family Guy quote list. Better than a merch blog: named editorial writer (Cathal Gunning), and cites season/episode/title for every entry. Used as a LEAD only. Its S/E attributions for 'Road to Rhode Island' (S2E13), 'And Then There Were Fewer' (S9E1) and 'Road to the North Pole' (S9E7) were each independently confirmed against Wikipedia, TVmaze, IMDb, TV Tropes, Fandom and TMDB — all matched. Only standalone lines were taken; setup lines and multi-part exchanges (e.g. the Brady Bunch bait-and-switch) were skipped as dialogue rather than quotes. Note the fetched page only exposed entries 25-16; the top 15 are lazy-loaded.
source_notes.ultimateclassicrock.com: User-supplied Beavis and Butt-Head list — 'Top 40 Beavis and Butt-Head One-Liners', Annie Zaleski, 2018-03-08, Townsquare Media. Bylined editorial writer; lists artist + song for all 40 entries. Critically, it lists NO season/episode numbers, and states the entries are sourced from video clips available online rather than episode records. Rather than invent episode numbers, these rows cite the music video itself. 39 rows taken: stage-direction entries (e.g. 'falls asleep in the middle of the video', 'sings Boston's More Than A Feeling') were skipped as not being quotes; 5 over-length lines were trimmed to their core; a few two-way exchanges were split into separate attributed rows.
source_notes.ranker.com: User-supplied King of the Hill list — '18 Times King Of The Hill Made A Really Good Point', Stephan Roget. Cites season/episode for most entries (no titles, no air dates), and its S7E7 and S8E2 attributions both checked out. Used as a LEAD ONLY, for two reasons. (1) CENSORED TEXT: the list bracket-substitutes words for ad-safety — 'Guns don't [terminate] people', 'Al Yankovic [took his own life]', 'why would anyone [ingest substances]', 'You either [go] or you don't', 'he knows for sure he gonna [perish]'. Those are the site's words, not the characters'. Any entry whose quote could not be sourced uncensored elsewhere was EXCLUDED rather than shipped with invented wording. (2) PARAPHRASE: even its uncensored entries drift — it renders the Christian-rock line as 'not making Christianity any better? You're making rock n roll worse', where the episode transcript reads 'not making Christianity better? You're just making rock and roll worse.' All shipped wording was taken from episode transcripts, Wikiquote and IMDb quote pages, not from the list.
source_notes.ranker.com \u2014 Simpsons list: User-supplied: 'The Simpsons Quotes We'll Never Get Tired Of', M. Muir, 29 entries. Much stronger than the same publisher's KOTH list — no censorship, and each entry carries season, episode AND title, many with full transcript context. BUT it contains a provable internal contradiction: it cites 'Bake him away, toys' as S5E2 'Cape Feare' (#20) AND 'No, it's the children who are wrong' as S5E2 'The Boy Who Knew Too Much' (#14). Both cannot be S5E2. Verification confirms Cape Feare IS S5E2 (aired 1993-10-07), so the Skinner line's citation is wrong and that entry was EXCLUDED pending its own verification. Its S7E21 and S5E2/Cape Feare attributions were independently confirmed. All shipped wording taken from IMDb quote pages and Simpsons Archive transcripts, not from the list's summaries.
source_notes.ranker.com \u2014 Kevin Malone list: User-supplied: 'The Best Things Kevin Malone Ever Said', credited to Ranker's 'Movie and TV Quotes' house account, 30 entries. Carries NO episode or season data whatsoever — every entry is bare text — so unlike the other Ranker lists it provided no attributions to check. Every episode below was researched and verified from scratch: 'The Incentive' S8E2 (Wikipedia, Wikidata, Rotten Tomatoes, Metacritic, TV Guide, Dunderpedia, TheTVDB) and the CPR cold open traced to the already-verified 'Stress Relief' S5E14 (Dunderpedia transcript). The list also paraphrases: it renders Kevin's CPR line as 'I can't do this forever' where the transcript reads 'I can't keep doing this forever', and drops 'Me think' from the famous line. All wording taken from Dunderpedia transcripts and IMDb quote pages. Entries whose home episode could not be verified were EXCLUDED per the standing rule — this includes most of the list, since single bare lines like 'I have very little patience for stupidity' or 'My name in high school was Kool-Aid Man' are not individually traceable without a per-line search each.
